Activation of pA-Tn5 results in factor-targeted tagmentation, generating fragments ready for PCR enrichment and DNA sequencing.

label: Plasmodium gametocyte detection assay
definition: An assay that detects Plasmodium gametocytes in a specimen.

label: malaria rapid diagnosis assay
definition: An assay that is quick and easy in the diagnosis of malaria by detecting evidence of malaria parasites (antigens) in human blood.

label: parasite detection assay
definition: An assay that detects parasite in a specimen.

label: feces microbiology assay
definition: An organism detection assay that detects microorganisms in a feces specimen.

label: blood assay
definition: An assay that has a blood specimen as evaulant.

label: falcivax rapid diagnostic test
definition: A parasite detection assay that can quickly establish the diagnosis of P. falciparum or P. vivax malaria infection by detecting the antigens in a person's blood.

label: optimal-IT rapid diagnostic test
definition: A parasite detection assay that is rapid, sensitive, and able to differentiate between P. falciparum and other malaria parasites.

label: urine assay
definition: An assay that has a urine specimen as evaluant.

label: parasite species identification by PCR assay
definition: A parasite detection by PCR assay that identifies the species of parasite.

label: parasite detection by PCR assay
definition: A parasite detection assay that uses PCR.

label: autofluorescence assay
definition: A fluorescence detection assay in which the light that is naturally emitted by a sample is visualized after excitation of the sample with light at a suitable wavelength.

label: autofluorescence microscopy assay
definition: An autofluorescence assay in which the light that is naturally emitted by a sample is visualized via microscopy after excitation of the sample with light at a suitable wavelength.

label: bulk assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing
definition: An assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing in which the sample that is sequenced is derived from a collection of cells, such as a tissue sample or entire cell culture, and therefore provides results representative of the aggregate of sample cells.

label: bulk RNA-seq assay
definition: An RNA-seq assay in which the sample that is sequenced is derived from a collection of cells, such as a tissue sample or entire cell culture, and therefore provides results representative of the aggregate of sample cells.

label: multiplexed fluorescent antibody imaging assay
definition: An imaging assay in which multiple cycles consisting of fluorescent labeling, imaging, and fluorophor deactivation are used to detect multiple proteins and their locations in a given sample of tissues or cells.

label: Cell DIVE multiplexed imaging assay
definition: A multiplexed fluorescent antibody imaging assay that involves an iterative staining, imaging and dye inactivation workflow for over 60 biomarkers on a single fixed tissue section.

label: co-detection by indexing assay
definition: A multiplexed fluorescent antibody imaging assay that involves a highly multiplexed analysis of up to 40 proteins in a tissue using cyclic detection of DNA-indexed antibody panels.

label: fluorescence in-situ hybridization assay
definition: An in-situ hybridization assay in which fluorescently labeled molecules are used to localize specific DNA or RNA sequences.

label: decoding amplified targeted transcripts with fluorescence in situ hybridization assay
definition: A fluorescence in-situ hybridization assay which involves multiplex in situ digital quantification of targeted RNA transcripts in fresh or frozen tissue providing an understanding of the spatial organization of different cell types.

label: imaging mass cytometry assay
definition: A cytometry time of flight assay in which molecules of interest on or in cells are imaged through a system in which samples are labeled with multiple different rare-earth tagged antibodies. The sample is then ablated with a laser and the labeled material is detected by cytometry time of flight mass spectrometry.

label: liquid chromatography mass spectrometry assay
definition: A mass spectrometry assay where a sample mixture is first separated by liquid chromatography before being converted into ions which are characterized by using mass spectrometry based on their mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

label: lightsheet fluorescence microscopy assay
definition: A fluorescence microscopy that involves capturing of photons emitted by fluorophores excited with a thin sheet of laser light in a sample only in a relatively narrow plane by a detection objective oriented perpendicularly to the light sheet and imaged onto a detection device such as a CCD camera.

label: matrix assisted laser desorption ionization imaging mass spectrometry assay
definition: A mass spectrometry assay that involves collection of spatially resolved mass spectra of a sample during microscopy where a pulse laser is used to produce both ionisation and vaporization. The sample is held in a matrix (such as dihydrobenzoic acid) to protect it from direct laser illumination and to separate the sample molecules. The spectra are used to visualise the spatial distribution of biomolecules by their molecular masses.

label: multiplexed ion beam imaging assay
definition: A cytometry time of flight assay in which molecules of interest on or in cells are imaged through a system in which samples are labeled with multiple different rare-earth tagged antibodies. A primary ion beam is ued to rasterize sections under vacuum, releasing showers of secondary ions detected by cytometry time of flight mass spectrometry.

label: nanospray desorption electrospray ionization assay
definition: A mass spectrometry assay that analyzes organic and biological molecules on a substrate by desorption of an analyte into a solvent bridge formed between two capillaries and the analysis surface. One capillary supplies solvent to create and maintain the bridge, while the second capillary transports the dissolved analyte from the bridge to the mass spectrometer. A high voltage applied between the inlet of mass spectrometer and the primary capillary creates a self-aspirating nanospray.

label: nanodroplet processing in one pot for trace samples assay
definition: A protein expression profiling assay in which proteomics sample processing is performed in nanoliter volumes. Flow cytometry or laser microdissection is employed to isolate a small population or single cells into a nanoPOTS chip. Then, liquid chromatography mass spectrometry is used to measure the global protein expression.

label: periodic acid-Schiff staining assay
definition: A histological assay which is used on tissue samples to demonstrate the presence of carbohydrates and carbohydrate compounds such as polysaccharides, mucin, glycogen, or fungal cell wall components.

label: single cell combinatorial indexing assay for transposase-accessessable chromatin using sequencing
definition: An assay for transposase-accessible chromatin that uses sequencing which involves single cell combinatorial indexing ('sci-') strategy where nucleic acids from each of many cells are uniquely tagged through several rounds of split-pool barcoding which enables identification of single cells without single cell isolation.

label: single-cell combinatorial indexing RNA sequencing assay
definition: A single-cell RNA sequencing assay that involves single cell combinatorial indexing ('sci-') strategy to profile the transcriptomes of single cells or nuclei without single cell isolation.

label: sequential fluorescence in-situ hybridization assay
definition: A fluorescence in-situ hybridization assay that involves ultra-resolution imaging of cell activity by targetting thousands of single molecules with fluorescent probes which find and hybridize with complementary DNA or RNA sequences in the tissue sample, thus enabling identification of those molecules directly in single cells with their spatial context preserved.

label: slide-seq assay
definition: An RNA-seq assay that involves transfer of RNA from tissue sections onto a surface covered in DNA-barcoded beads with known positions, allowing the locations of the RNA to be inferred by sequencing.

label: single-nucleus chromatin accessibility and mRNA expression sequencing assay
definition: A single-nucleus RNA sequencing assay that involves joint profiling of accessible chromatin and RNA within the same cells which enables direct matching of transcriptional regulation to its outputs.

label: single-nucleus RNA sequencing assay
definition: A RNA-seq assay that is used for profiling gene expression in individual nuclei with optimized next generation sequencing (NGS) technologies. This allows the RNA-seq profiling of cell types that are more vulnerable to the tissue dissociation process, and that are therefore underrepresented in the final data set in single cell sequencing.

label: gas chromatography mass spectrometry assay
definition: A mass spectrometry assay combining mass spectrometry and gas chromatography for the qualitative as well as quantitative determination of compounds.

label: SOMAscan assay
definition: An analyte assay that uses aptamers to detect protein analytes in serum.

label: Olink assay
definition: A proximity extension assay that uses quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) technology to determine the concentration/presence of proteins using a high-multiplex, high-throughput protein biomarker platform. The assay utilizes two distinct oligonucleotide-labeled antibodies (‘probes’) that bind at different sites for each detected protein. When the two probes are in close proximity, a new PCR target sequence is formed by a proximity-dependent DNA polymerization event. The resulting sequence is subsequently detected and quantified using standard real-time PCR.

label: proximity extension assay

label: antigen detection by cytometric bead array assay

label: antibody detection by cytometric bead array assay

definition: An assay that evaluates a blood specimen for antibodies currently being produced by lymphocytes in the specimen, by separating peripheral blood mononuclear cells, culturing them, and then collecting the supernatant containing the antibodies secreted from those cells.

label: tyramide signal amplification sequencing assay
definition: A DNA sequencing assay that uses tyramide signal amplification (TSA) to assess distance of DNA regions to a targeted nuclear compartment or protein, typically on a scale of 100-1000 nm.

label: DNA adenine methyltransferase identification assay
definition: An assay for identifying DNA binding sites for a protein by fusing it to Dam methylase, and expressing it so that bound DNA gets methylated. The methylated DNA can then be isolated and analyzed.

label: DamID-seq
definition: A DNA adenine methyltransferase identification (DamID) assay in which DamID-generated DNA fragments undergo high-throughput sequencing to determine a protein's DNA-binding site.

label: nucleolus-associated domain sequencing assay
definition: A DNA sequencing assay in which nucleoli are isolated and the DNA associated with them is sequenced to identify nucleoli-associating domains.

label: transposase-mediated analysis of chromatin looping assay
definition: A DNA sequencing assay designed to detect interacting genomic regions. Rather than the traditional Hi-C approach of digestion and proximity ligation, the procedure involves transposase-mediated insertion of an oligonucleotide linker between the pair of interacting regions.

label: split-pool recognition of interactions and tag extension assay
definition: A sequencing assay designed to detect multi-way interactions between nucleic acids. The procedure involves crosslinking nuclei, and then splitting the lysate among wells in a 96-well or other multi-well plate. A different barcode is ligated to the fragments in each well, and the lysates are pooled together again. This sequence of splitting, tagging, and re-combining is repeated several times so that fragments with the same sequences of barcodes represent fragments that have co-associated throughout the experiment. Finally, a sequencing library is constructed and high-throughput sequencing is performed.

label: DNA split-pool recognition of interactions and tag extension assay
definition: A split-pool recognition of interactions and tag extension (SPRITE) assay that only assays interactions between regions of genomic DNA.

label: RNA-DNA split-pool recognition of interactions and tag extension assay
definition: A split-pool recognition of interactions and tag extension (SPRITE) assay in which RNA in the cross-linked complexes is converted to cDNA before the initial splitting step, allowing analysis of RNA-DNA interactions.

label: genome architecture mapping assay
definition: A DNA sequencing assay designed to analyze 3D chromatin structure without relying on digestion and ligation. The procedure involves cryosectioning samples in random orientation, and then single nuclear profiles are isolated by laser microdissection. Each nuclear profile then undergoes high-throughput sequencing, and subsequent analysis can generate a matrix of inferred proximity between genomic regions.

label: venous blood microbiology assay
definition: A blood microbiology assay that detects a microorganism in a venous blood specimen.

label: detection technique
definition: An assay (A) that is part of another assay (B), where the target entities of A and B are disjoint, and the target entity of A is a proxy for the target of assay B.

label: placental blood microbiology assay

label: linked-read sequencing assay
